practice.title: Math guided practice · Add and subtract signed fractions

items.prompt: A temperature is -4 degrees C and rises 8 degrees. New temperature?
items.answer: 4 degrees C

items.prompt: A bank balance is $12.50. A $20.75 purchase is recorded. Find the new balance and explain its sign.
items.answer: -$8.25; negative means the account is $8.25 below zero.

practice.title: Science
contexts: W1 data: A fictional comparison records temperature before and after a controlled warming step. Trial A: 21 temperature in degrees C; Trial B: 29 temperature in degrees C. These are invented assessment data, not a claim about a real investigation.

items.prompt: Use W1 data. Which trial has the higher recorded value, and by how much?
items.answer: Trial B; 8 temperature in degrees C.

items.prompt: Use W1 data. State one observation without claiming its cause.
items.answer: Trial B recorded 29 versus 21 in A; accept an accurate description without an unsupported causal claim.

practice.title: Art
practice.passage: Notation records selected musical features. Values depend on the stated system and context. Count durations rather than assuming all symbols last the same time.

items.prompt: Why state the notation system?
items.answer: So symbols can be interpreted as intended durations and sounds.

items.prompt: Notate a four-beat pattern and translate durations into a fraction model. Use precise vocabulary, two supporting reasons or observations, and a limitation.
items.answer: Look for a relevant completed activity, an accurate concept, evidence or an example, and a reasoned explanation/revision. Accept varied justified responses. Do not grade beliefs or private experiences.

practice.title: Human Sciences
practice.passage: Philosophy examines questions about knowledge, reality, meaning, and how to live. A claim states a position; a reason supports it. Asking for reasons differs from attacking a person.

items.prompt: How do a claim and a reason differ?
items.answer: A claim states a position; a reason explains support for it.

items.prompt: Sort factual, preference, and philosophical questions; discuss one using a claim and reason. Use precise vocabulary, two supporting reasons or observations, and a limitation.
items.answer: Look for a relevant completed activity, an accurate concept, evidence or an example, and a reasoned explanation/revision. Accept varied justified responses. Do not grade beliefs or private experiences.
